notes.meaning: Worldly rulers love to push people around and enjoy being flattered with grand titles like "benefactors." Jesus warned His followers that chasing power and prestige belongs to pagan kings, not to His kingdom. True greatness comes from actually helping people, not from ruling over them.

Jesus told His disciples that their community must operate under totally different rules. Anyone who wants to be great must take the lower place, like the youngest member of the family who does the hard work. Leading others in the church means taking the humble role of a servant.

In normal society, the guest sitting at the dinner table is honored above the servant waiting on them. Yet Jesus, who is the Master, spent His time among the disciples serving them and caring for their needs. If the Lord Himself acts as a servant, His followers have no right to act proud.

Jesus warmly praised the disciples for staying loyal to Him during all His hardships and trials. Even though they had many flaws and misunderstandings, He kindly recognized their faithfulness in sticking by His side.

Just as the Father granted a kingdom to Jesus through His suffering, Jesus promised a share in that kingdom to His faithful followers. They will enjoy a feast of close fellowship with Him and receive positions of honor and authority to judge God's people. Their reward for humble service on earth will be great glory in heaven.

Jesus warned Simon Peter that Satan had asked for permission from God to shake all the disciples violently, like grain in a sieve. The devil wanted to crush them with fear and prove that their faith was empty chaff. Satan cannot touch believers without God's permission, but he constantly looks for chances to attack them.

Jesus assured Peter that He had personally prayed for him, so that his faith would not be completely destroyed by the trial. Although Peter would stumble badly, Jesus knew he would repent and return. Once restored, Peter's job was to encourage and strengthen the rest of the disciples.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Jesus praying for Peter alone and giving him the task of strengthening all the other apostles points to Peter's unique authority and leadership over the whole church.

notes.meaning: Peter boldly declared that he was prepared to go with Jesus anywhere, even to jail or to the grave. He meant what he said with all his heart, but he relied too much on his own strength. Human confidence often collapses when real danger arrives.

Jesus bluntly told Peter that before morning came and the rooster crowed, Peter would deny even knowing Him three times. The Lord knew Peter's hidden weakness far better than Peter knew himself. Christ sees our upcoming failures and still offers grace to restore us.

Jesus reminded the disciples of their earlier preaching trip, when they carried no money bag, extra food, or spare shoes. When He asked if they lacked anything back then, they answered that they had everything they needed. Remembering God's past care gives us confidence for future difficulties.

Jesus explained that the season of peaceful acceptance was ending and very dangerous times were arriving. From now on, they would need to carry regular supplies, like money and bags, and be prepared for fierce opposition. His vivid words urged them to be fully ready for intense trials ahead.

differ.view: Jesus used the sword as a figure of speech to warn the disciples of severe spiritual warfare and temptations ahead, not to command physical combat.
Jesus was giving practical advice for dangerous travels after His departure, showing that self-defense against criminals or wild beasts is lawful.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Jesus approved of carrying weapons for lawful self-defense, even though He prohibited using them to prevent His arrest.

notes.meaning: Jesus explained that Bible prophecy had to be completed in Him, especially the verse saying He would be treated like a common criminal. His earthly work was reaching its final goal in the suffering of the cross. Believers can take comfort knowing that Christ's pain was not an accident, but part of God's redemptive plan.

The disciples took His words about weapons literally and showed Him two swords they already carried. Jesus answered, "That is enough," shutting down the conversation because they had missed His point. Two swords could never defend against an army, and Jesus did not intend to fight an earthly battle.

Jesus left the upper room and walked out to the Mount of Olives, just as He regularly did to pray in peace. The remaining eleven disciples followed Him into the quiet night. Judas knew this habit well, which allowed him to guide the arrest party there later.

When they reached the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus urged the disciples to pray so they would not give in to temptation. He knew a severe spiritual storm was about to hit them. Prayer is the best defense when trials threaten to sweep us away.

Jesus walked a short distance past the disciples, about as far as someone could throw a stone. He dropped to His knees on the cold ground to pour out His heart to the Father. He needed solitude to face the deep agony coming upon Him.

Jesus pleaded that if it were possible, the bitter cup of suffering and divine judgment for sin might be taken away from Him. Yet He immediately yielded completely, asking that the Father's will be done rather than His own human desires. His obedience shows the ultimate example of submitting to God even when it costs everything.

An angel came from heaven to give strength to Jesus during His extreme distress. In His human nature, Christ was pushed to the absolute edge of endurance and welcomed this heavenly help. It was part of His deep humiliation that the Lord of glory was supported by one of His own created angels.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some ancient manuscripts leave out verses 43 and 44, leading scholars to debate whether Luke wrote them originally or if early copyists added them from oral tradition.

notes.meaning: Gripped by immense anguish as He faced the burden of sin, Jesus prayed with even greater urgency and intensity. His physical and emotional strain became so severe that His sweat fell like thick clots of blood onto the ground. This intense struggle shows the terrible cost of redeeming sinners.

When Jesus finished praying and returned to His disciples, He found them fast asleep. Their spirits were completely drained and exhausted by the deep grief and sorrow of that night. Even when people care, human strength easily fails in the darkest moments.

Jesus woke the disciples and asked why they were sleeping instead of watching. He commanded them once more to get up and pray so they would not fall into temptation when the enemy struck. Giving in to spiritual tiredness leaves us unprotected against sin.

Before Jesus had finished speaking, a large armed mob arrived in the garden, guided by Judas, one of the Twelve. Judas stepped forward to greet Jesus with a kiss, using an ordinary sign of love and friendship as the signal to hand Him over to His enemies. Betrayal hurts deepest when it comes from someone who claimed to be a close friend.
